universes.name: The Sacred Timeline
universes.blurb: Marvel Studios' primary reality. Every MCU film, every Disney+ series, the Netflix Defenders shows and the ABC/Hulu Marvel Television slate have all been folded into this one continuity.

universes.name: The First Family's World
universes.blurb: A retro-futurist 1960s Earth where the Fantastic Four are its only superheroes — and its Galactus arrives without an Avengers to answer. Separate from the Sacred Timeline until Doomsday.

universes.name: The Illuminati's Earth
universes.blurb: The polished, sunlit reality Doctor Strange and America Chavez fall into — governed by an Illuminati whose members are alternate versions of heroes from five different franchises.

universes.name: The Time Variance Authority
universes.blurb: Not an Earth at all. A bureaucracy sitting outside the flow of time, pruning branched realities into the Void — the junkyard where erased variants go to be eaten by Alioth.

universes.name: The Watcher's Multiverse
universes.blurb: Uatu the Watcher's vantage point over an infinite fan of branch realities, each one a single decision away from the Sacred Timeline.

universes.name: The Zombie Reality
universes.blurb: A branch where the Quantum Realm virus won. Grown out of the What If...? episode 'What If... Zombies?!' into its own TV-MA continuity.

universes.name: Peter Parker's Other First Year
universes.blurb: A deliberately re-branched origin: Norman Osborn, not Tony Stark, mentors a newly-bitten Peter Parker.

universes.name: The Raimi Universe
universes.blurb: Tobey Maguire's New York. Organic web-shooters, a Daily Bugle run at full volume, and the first Spider-Man trilogy to make the modern superhero film viable.

universes.name: The Amazing Universe
universes.blurb: Andrew Garfield's New York — Oscorp-centric, Gwen Stacy at its heart, and cut short after two films by Sony's reboot into the MCU.

universes.name: Sony's Spider-Man Universe
universes.blurb: Six films of Spider-Man's rogues without a Spider-Man. Venom, Morbius, Madame Web and Kraven share a reality that brushes the MCU twice and never merges with it.

universes.name: The Spider-Verse Hub
universes.blurb: Miles Morales' Brooklyn — and the anchor point from which Into/Across the Spider-Verse tour dozens of other spider-realities.

universes.name: Peter B. Parker's Earth
universes.blurb: A worn-down, divorced, 38-year-old Spider-Man's reality.

universes.name: Gwen Stacy's Earth
universes.blurb: Spider-Gwen's watercolour world, where Peter Parker died and Gwen got bitten.

universes.name: Nueva York, 2099
universes.blurb: Miguel O'Hara's future, and the headquarters of the Spider Society.

universes.name: Spider-Man Noir's Earth
universes.blurb: A monochrome 1933 in permanent black-and-white.

universes.name: Peni Parker's Earth
universes.blurb: An anime reality where SP//dr is piloted by a girl and a radioactive spider together.

universes.name: Spider-Ham's Earth
universes.blurb: A Looney Tunes physics reality inhabited by Peter Porker.

universes.name: Spider-Punk's Earth
universes.blurb: Hobie Brown's anarchist London, rendered as a moving collage of zines.

universes.name: Mumbattan
universes.blurb: Pavitr Prabhakar's India — introduced in the 2004 Spider-Man: India comic.

universes.name: Jessica Drew's Earth
universes.blurb: Spider-Woman's reality, per the Across the Spider-Verse screenplay.

universes.name: The 1967 Cartoon
universes.blurb: The reality of the original ABC Spider-Man cartoon — and the source of the internet's most reproduced meme.

universes.name: Toei's Japanese Spider-Man
universes.blurb: Takuya Yamashiro's 1978 tokusatsu reality, giant mecha and all. Cameos as a sketch in Miles' notebook.

universes.name: The Fox Mutant Timeline
universes.blurb: Twenty years and thirteen films of X-Men, from Bryan Singer's 2000 original through Deadpool 2 — the timeline Deadpool & Wolverine finally canonised as an anchor reality.

universes.name: The Erased Timeline
universes.blurb: The original X-Men trilogy's dark future — the continuity Days of Future Past deliberately unwrote in 1973.

universes.name: Logan's Last Road
universes.blurb: 2029. Mutants have effectively stopped being born. A separate, terminal branch.

universes.name: The New Mutants
universes.blurb: The last film released under the Fox banner, and the only one Marvel has never assigned a canonical reality number.

universes.name: Legion
universes.blurb: David Haller's reality — or possibly his delusion. Noah Hawley's FX series keeps that deliberately unresolved.

universes.name: The Gifted
universes.blurb: A post-X-Men America where the X-Men have vanished and the Mutant Underground is all that's left.

universes.name: The '90s Animated Universe
universes.blurb: Shared home of X-Men: The Animated Series and Spider-Man: The Animated Series — and, thirty years later, of X-Men '97.

universes.name: The Daywalker's World
universes.blurb: New Line's Blade trilogy plus the 2006 Spike TV series — the films that proved a Marvel adaptation could open a movie.

universes.name: Fox's Fantastic Four
universes.blurb: Tim Story's two films — and the source of the Human Torch who turns up trapped in the Void two decades later.

universes.name: Fant4stic
universes.blurb: Josh Trank's body-horror-adjacent reboot, disowned by nearly everyone involved.

universes.name: The Corman Cut
universes.blurb: A Fantastic Four film made in under a month to retain rights, never released, and bootlegged into legend.

universes.name: Hell's Kitchen (2003)
universes.blurb: Ben Affleck's Daredevil and Jennifer Garner's Elektra. Garner's return in Deadpool & Wolverine made it a canonical anchor reality.

universes.name: The Rider's Reality
universes.blurb: Nicolas Cage's Johnny Blaze, across two films with no connection to the MCU's Ghost Rider.

universes.name: Ang Lee's Hulk
universes.blurb: A comic-panel-framed psychodrama that Marvel Studios quietly stepped around five years later.

universes.name: The Bixby Hulk
universes.blurb: Five CBS seasons and three NBC reunion films. For a generation this was Marvel on television.

universes.name: Dolph Lundgren's Punisher
universes.blurb: No skull, no US theatrical release.

universes.name: Thomas Jane's Punisher
universes.blurb: Lionsgate's Tampa-set revenge film.

universes.name: War Zone
universes.blurb: Lexi Alexander's hyper-violent stand-alone reboot.

universes.name: Howard's Cleveland
universes.blurb: The first film based on a Marvel Comics property produced under the modern Marvel banner — and for decades its most notorious.

universes.name: Matt Salinger's Captain America
universes.blurb: Albert Pyun's $3M Cap, shelved for two years and released to video.

universes.name: The CBS Captain America
universes.blurb: Two 1979 TV movies with a motorcycle-riding Steve Rogers.

universes.name: The Nexus Swamp
universes.blurb: A Marvel horror film that skipped US theatres for the Sci Fi Channel.

universes.name: San Fransokyo
universes.blurb: Walt Disney Animation's take on a little-known Marvel team — and the only Marvel property to win the Best Animated Feature Oscar.

universes.name: The Marvel Animated Universe
universes.blurb: Disney XD's shared continuity: Ultimate Spider-Man, Avengers Assemble, Agents of S.M.A.S.H. and Guardians of the Galaxy.

universes.name: Earth's Mightiest Heroes
universes.blurb: The shared reality of Wolverine and the X-Men and The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes — long held up as the most faithful Avengers adaptation.

universes.name: The Spectacular Spider-Man
universes.blurb: Greg Weisman's two-season series, cancelled by a rights change rather than by ratings.

universes.name: The Marvel Productions Universe
universes.blurb: The 1980s Saturday-morning reality of Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends and the 1982 Incredible Hulk.

universes.name: Helstrom
universes.blurb: The final Marvel Television production, developed as an MCU tie-in and then explicitly severed from it.

universes.name: Unassigned Realities
universes.blurb: Adaptations Marvel's own Multiverse index has never given a number to.

edges: Willem Dafoe returns as Norman Osborn / Green Goblin, pulled out of Earth-96283 mid-fall.
Alfred Molina returns as Otto Octavius, grabbed from the moment before his death.
Thomas Haden Church returns as Flint Marko / Sandman.
Rhys Ifans returns as Curt Connors / the Lizard.
Jamie Foxx returns as Max Dillon / Electro.
Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker crosses over as the Earth-96283 variant.
Andrew Garfield's Peter Parker crosses over as the Earth-120703 variant — and catches MJ.
Charlie Cox appears as Matt Murdock, Peter's attorney — the Netflix continuity's first on-screen entry into a Marvel Studios film.
J.K. Simmons returns as J. Jonah Jameson in the post-credits — recast from Earth-96283 into the MCU.
The mid-credits scene yanks Eddie Brock into the MCU, where he watches Jameson's broadcast unmasking Spider-Man.
Eddie is snapped back to Earth-688B but leaves a fragment of the symbiote behind in an MCU bar.
The post-credits scene drags Michael Keaton's Adrian Toomes / Vulture out of the MCU and into the SSU via a No Way Home-style spell.
Direct continuation of Eddie Brock and the symbiote's story.
Direct continuation, closing the Venom trilogy.
Shares the SSU's continuity and Spider-mythology (Ezekiel Sims, the Parker family) without a character crossover.
The final SSU film; shares the reality without crossing into any other entry.
Wesley Snipes returns as Blade, twenty years after Trinity.
Jennifer Garner returns as Elektra from Earth-701306.
Chris Evans returns — as Johnny Storm, not Steve Rogers.
Dafne Keen returns as Laura / X-23, now grown, from Logan's timeline.
Tyler Mane returns as Sabretooth and Ray Park as Toad, from the 2000 original.
Picks up Wade Wilson's story directly, then hands him to the TVA.
Built on the TVA and the Void — the machinery Loki season 1 established.
Wolverine finally wears the comic-accurate yellow-and-blue the animated series made iconic.
Canonises Earth-10005 as an 'anchor reality' — the Fox films are no longer erased.
Hayley Atwell's Captain Carter steps out of the animated multiverse and onto Earth-838 in live action.
Anson Mount returns as Black Bolt, from the 2017 ABC series, as an Illuminati member.
Patrick Stewart returns as Charles Xavier — in the animated series' hoverchair.
Xavier's Earth-838 introduction is scored with the 1992 animated series theme.
Lashana Lynch's Maria Rambeau is Earth-838's Captain Marvel.
Directly continues Wanda's Darkhold corruption and her search for Billy and Tommy.
Names Strange's botched spell as the trigger for the incursions.
John Krasinski's Reed Richards cameo on Earth-838, three years before Marvel Studios' own Fantastic Four.
Direct continuation — Across picks up Miles' story and expands it to hundreds of realities.
The post-credits sting sends Miguel to Earth-67 and recreates the pointing meme.
Spider-Man Unlimited's design recurs among Spider Society background variants.
Miguel's screens replay live-action footage from the Raimi films.
Live-action Amazing Spider-Man footage appears in the Spider Society's canon-event archive.
Earth-688 — the Venom films' reality — is visible on the Spider Society's multiverse display.
Vincent D'Onofrio returns as Wilson Fisk, carrying the Netflix Kingpin straight into Marvel Studios canon.
Picks up Maya Lopez immediately after the Hawkeye finale.
Kingpin and Matt Murdock both appear, settling the Netflix shows' canon status.
Direct continuation of Murdock and Fisk after the Netflix finale.
Continues Fisk's mayoral campaign, set up in Echo.
Jon Bernthal returns as Frank Castle across season 1.
Krysten Ritter returns as Jessica Jones in season 2 — her first appearance since The Defenders.
Frank Castle's Born Again arc continues into this stand-alone special rather than into season 2.
Bernthal's Punisher returns to lead his own story for the first time since the Netflix series ended.
Charlie Cox's Daredevil gets a multi-episode comic arc — and a yellow suit.
Tim Roth returns as Emil Blonsky / Abomination, fourteen years later.
Team-up miniseries uniting Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist.
Frank Castle spun out of Daredevil season 2 into his own series.
Luke Cage was introduced in Jessica Jones season 1.
'The Well' handles the cleanup after the Asgardian battle in Greenwich.
'Turn, Turn, Turn' aired days after the film and detonates the same HYDRA reveal across the series.
Season 2–3 track the vibranium fallout and the road to the Sokovia Accords.
The season 5 finale plays out against the Snap.
Inhumans spun directly out of the series' season 3 Terrigenesis arc.
Shares the S.H.I.E.L.D. founding mythology; Peggy Carter runs through both.
Introduces Robbie Reyes as Ghost Rider — a separate character and continuity from Nicolas Cage's Johnny Blaze.
Picks up Peggy Carter's life after Steve Rogers goes into the ice.
Establishes Edwin Jarvis, Howard Stark and the pre-history of J.A.R.V.I.S.
Reveals that Tony Stark's visit to Ross was a ploy to keep Banner off the Avengers roster.
Coulson's detour on the way to New Mexico, immediately before Thor.
A couple scavenge a Chitauri rifle from the wreckage of the Battle of New York.
The one-shot's reception is what got the series greenlit.
Trevor Slattery, still playing the Mandarin, in Seagate Prison.
Sets up the real Ten Rings — and Slattery's return seven years later.
Peter Parker's first days back from Berlin, days after the airport fight.
Picks up Earth-92131 directly after the 1997 finale, same reality, several original voice actors.
The Watcher's multiverse and the TVA's pruning are two views of the same branching.
He Who Remains, introduced in Loki's finale, returns as Kang the Conqueror.
Agatha Harkness, last seen hexed into 'Agnes', returns as protagonist.
Wanda's apparent death and the Darkhold's destruction are treated as settled backstory.
'What If... Captain Carter Were the First Avenger?' branches at the serum injection.
'What If... T'Challa Became a Star-Lord?' branches at Yondu's abduction.
'What If... Ultron Won?' branches at Age of Ultron's climax.
'What If... Killmonger Rescued Tony Stark?' branches in the Afghan convoy.
Grown out of the 'What If... Zombies?!' episode into its own four-part series.
Shorts set in the gap between the two Guardians films.
Thunderbolts* ends with the New Avengers detecting the Fantastic Four's craft entering Earth-616 airspace.
References Sam Wilson's Captain America and a naming dispute over 'the Avengers'.
Tim Blake Nelson returns as Samuel Sterns / the Leader, seventeen years after the seed was planted.
Continues Thaddeus Ross's arc — now recast, and now President.
The adamantium comes from Tiamut's emerged body — the Celestial Island left at Eternals' end.
Mahershala Ali's Blade speaks in the mid-credits as Dane Whitman reaches for the Ebony Blade.
Wong, Carol Danvers and Bruce Banner examine the Ten Rings and pick up a signal.
Trevor Slattery's fake-Mandarin story finally collides with the real one.
Kamala and Carol swap places through the bangle in the finale's post-credits scene.
Kamala's bangle is tied to Kree and Noor-dimension mythology.
Monica wakes in a reality where Kelsey Grammer's Beast is waiting — the Fox mutants, entering.
Continues Riri Williams' story after her introduction in Wakanda Forever.
Simon Williams' Hollywood satire sits alongside She-Hulk as Marvel Television's other fourth-wall-adjacent comedy.
Set in the gap between Civil War and Infinity War; the post-credits jumps past Endgame.
Picks up a Peter Parker nobody remembers, after the spell erased him from the world.
Charlie Cox's Daredevil crosses over from Marvel Television into the Spider-Man films.
Time travel unwrites the original trilogy's future — and the trilogy's own continuity with it.
Bridges the First Class cast and the original cast into a single, rewritten timeline.
Direct continuation inside the reset timeline.
Closes out the First Class-era timeline.
A separate, terminal near-future branch rather than a continuation.
Essex Corp ties it loosely to the Mr. Sinister thread seeded in the main series.
Wade Wilson is rebooted from scratch; the film opens by mocking the earlier version.
Direct continuation, plus a time-travel coda that undoes the previous film's worst outcomes.
Direct continuation, resolving the Phoenix arc.
Set after the original trilogy, with Jean Grey haunting Logan.
MTV's CG series is set between the first two Raimi films, with Peter still in college.
Spike TV series set in the same reality after the films.
Spin-off continuing Elektra Natchios after her death in Daredevil.
Direct continuation with the same Johnny Blaze, a new creative team, and a harder tone.
First of three NBC reunion films; introduces Thor to network television.
Second reunion film; introduces Daredevil, played by Rex Smith.
Final reunion film; kills David Banner.
Picks up immediately after the film.
Both series share Earth-8096; characters and continuity cross between them.
Disney XD's shared animated continuity — Spider-Man crosses into the Avengers' series repeatedly.
A deliberately re-branched origin: Norman Osborn takes the mentor role Tony Stark held.
Anthology of Wakandan history across three millennia, confirmed Sacred Timeline canon.
Bridges Vol. 2 and Vol. 3, and explains how Kevin Bacon ends up on Knowhere.
Introduces Jack Russell, Elsa Bloodstone and Man-Thing into the Sacred Timeline.
Direct continuation — and the Time Heist that creates the branched realities Loki inherits.
Cloak and Dagger appear in Runaways season 3, the only Marvel Television cross-show crossover of its era.
